This is configuration-only: [docs/scripts/translate-chrome.ts](docs/scripts/translate-chrome.ts) already supplies a source-value allowlist to the shared guard, and focused memory tests cover that contract. The examples split into two categories: universal technical terms such as “CSS,” and locale-specific legitimate identity translations such as Spanish “Base” or Ukrainian “Menu.” Marking all examples globally verbatim would conceal real misses like Spanish “Guide,” so I’m checking whether chrome strings can carry per-locale policies and will encode only defensible identities.

The shared adapter already has the right per-locale policy model, while the chrome wrapper currently reduces it to an all-or-nothing `Set`. I’m narrowing the missing identities from the actual run output and cache state so the fix preserves strict retries for genuinely untranslated labels such as Spanish “Guide” and “CDN & distribution.”
